> Author: researcher (vfx-gap-research workflow) · claude-sonnet-5-5 · low · 2026-10-12

# Gap fill: clutter, coverage, overdraw, brightness, ally toning

Scope: first-run files `p3-scene.md` (P3) and `p9-p10-p11-access-perf-roblox.md` (P9). Gaps (a) screen coverage, (b) overdraw budgets, (c) effect vs environment brightness, (d) how many simultaneous effects, (e) ally effect toning.
Evidence levels: study | preprint | industry practice | spec | inference. Fetch tool returns a model-made summary of each page, so numbers are as returned; PDFs (BT.2408-8, Bungie deck) were read as raw text with pdftotext.
Headline: no studio (Destiny, Apex, CoD, Overwatch, Fortnite, Wild Rift, Genshin) published a number for screen-coverage %, overdraw layers or particle GPU ms that this search tool could reach. The numbers we did find are vendor tool docs, vision-science clutter studies, ITU/Microsoft/W3C display standards and two official shipped ally-toning settings. Everything else is marked "no number found".

## 1. Search count used

WebSearch: 12 / 15 (standard mode). WebFetch: about 58 calls, over the soft cap of 40 given in the brief; roughly 20 of them were failures (403, 404, JS-only shells, redirects, size cap). One 19 MB GDC PDF exceeded the WebFetch size limit and was fetched with curl into the scratchpad, then read with pdftotext (read only; nothing kept in the repo).

## 3. Gap-by-gap results

### GAP: (a) screen coverage of effects (% of screen)

Status: STILL OPEN for effect coverage %. [V: confirmed - 5.6 to 14%, 6.6 to 13%, and the 1.4% / 17% example frames re-read in ITU BT.2408-8] Proxies only. Best number found: 5.6 to 14% of pixels sit above diffuse white in graded HDR frames (G17), which is a highlight share, not an effect share.

| finding | numbers | evidence level | source ids |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No studio effect-coverage percentage found in any source opened. Searches aimed at Destiny, Apex, CoD, Overwatch, Fortnite, Wild Rift, Genshin returned no such figure. | no number found | n/a | G16, G22, G23 |
| Destiny uses screen coverage as a control signal, not as a fixed cap: a translucent particle's opacity and size are adjusted by its screen coverage (from distance, size, frame resolution); jittered near fade thins a system as coverage grows; a "perf hammer" thins the most expensive systems when GPU time is bad, picked by an offline report and a runtime coverage check. | no threshold number in the deck | industry practice (Bungie, GDC 2018; pre-2020) | G16 |
| In 107 HDR images graded to 1000 cd/m2, 99% of images have 5.6 to 14% of pixels above 203 cd/m2 (reference white); 95% have 6.6 to 13%. Example frames: 1.4% (highlights only) and 17% (bright sky). Candidate use for us: the share of a frame allowed to exceed the stage's diffuse white is single digits to low teens of percent. This is a broadcast stills statistic, not about effects. | 5.6 to 14% (99% CI); 6.6 to 13% (95% CI); 1.4% and 17% examples | study (ITU annex analysis) for the broadcast number; inference for the effect budget | G17 |
| Flash area limits (25% of the screen under ITU; WCAG 0.006 sr) apply to flashing only and already sit in P9 rows "Flash area, WCAG" and "Flash area, ITU". They give a hard safety ceiling on the area of a repeated bright pulse, not a design budget. | 25% of screen (first-run S2) | spec | P9 S1, S2 |
| Roblox engine side: particle size costs fill-rate (more screen pixels covered = more GPU cost). No pixel or % cap in the docs. | no number found | spec | G27 |
| Clutter studies (below, gap d) show cost to search time scales with clutter score and set size, not with a coverage % threshold. | see (d) | study | G08 |

### GAP: (c) brightness ratios between effects and environment (stops, nits)

Status: PARTLY FILLED. Display-standard reference levels found; no game studio "effects X stops above scene" rule found. Best number: HDR reference white 203 cd/m2 against a 1000 cd/m2 reference peak, about 2.3 stops of highlight headroom (G17, our arithmetic). [V: confirmed - log2(1000/203) = 2.30 and log2(203/26) = 2.96; ExposureCompensation 1 = one stop is an inference from the doc] [V: corrected - mapping display-referred HDR broadcast ratios onto Roblox SDR effects is inference; PARTLY FILLED holds only for the display-standard levels, and an "effects X stops above scene" rule stays OPEN.]

| finding | numbers | evidence level | source ids |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ITU HDR production reference: a 100% reflectance white (also "Graphics White") sits at 203 cd/m2; an 18% grey card at 26 cd/m2; reference display peak 1000 cd/m2. Our arithmetic: 1000 / 203 = 4.9x, about 2.3 stops of headroom above diffuse white; 203 / 26 = 7.8x, about 3.0 stops from mid grey to white. Candidate model for the agent: stage diffuse white as the reference, effect focus allowed up to roughly 2 stops above it, treated as a hypothesis. | 203, 26, 1000 cd/m2; 4.9x (2.3 stops); 7.8x (3.0 stops) | spec for the levels; inference for the effects mapping | G17 |
| Measured diffuse white varies a lot in real content: live HLG broadcast mean 75% HLG, standard deviation about 8.3%, about 123 to 345 cd/m2 (assuming a 1000 cd/m2 signal); PQ image set mean about 60% PQ, standard deviation 11%, about 80 to 700 cd/m2. Meaning: a fixed absolute brightness for effects does not transfer between scenes; relative-to-local-white does. | 123 to 345 cd/m2; 80 to 700 cd/m2 | study (ITU annex analysis) | G17 |
| Microsoft HDR guidance: nominal reference white 80 nits; users commonly set SDR reference white around 200 nits on desktop HDR monitors; scRGB value 12.5 = 1000 nits. | 80 nits; about 200 nits; 12.5 = 1000 nits | spec (platform holder) | G18 |
| Roblox: Lighting.ExposureCompensation has range -5 to 5 and 1 means twice the exposure (so 1 unit = 1 stop); applied before tonemap. ParticleEmitter.Brightness only scales emitted light when LightInfluence is 0. BloomEffect.Threshold: 1 = only pure white blooms, 0 = all colours bloom. No HDR output statement in the four docs checked (possibly SDR only on most clients; unconfirmed). | -5 to 5; 1 = 2x exposure | spec | G27 |
| W3C: graphics needed to understand content need at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours. Use as a floor for gameplay-critical cues (pickup, hazard edge) against their local background. It is a static-graphics rule on relative luminance and says nothing about moving effects. | 3:1 minimum | spec (applied by inference) | G19 |
| Named-artist practice, single source each, no studio: a per-environment "VFX Multiplier" scales particle emissive so one effect set fits many lighting presets; per-emitter multipliers only for small items like embers, used sparingly. Another artist divides emissive by eye adaptation to keep apparent brightness stable across exposure. No numbers. | no number found | industry practice (tier C, single source each) | G20, G21 |
| No source opened states an effects-to-scene brightness ratio in stops or nits for a shipped game. | no number found | n/a | none |

### GAP: (d) how many simultaneous effects before clutter

Status: PARTLY FILLED. Vision-science numbers on how clutter slows search; capacity limits near four; no studio count of simultaneous effects; no game-effect clutter study found. Best number: with highly cluttered backgrounds, find-the-target time rose 28 to 130% over a blank background, and the clutter effect was weak at set size 4 (G08). [V: confirmed - the four search-time pairs match] [V: corrected - the authors suggest the effect faded at set size 4 because the task was too easy (few locations, little eye movement); it does not show that 4 items is a clutter-safe count and must not support a "4 effects" rule. The +28% to +130% is correlational across background types (r 0.55 to 0.66) on static video-call images.]

| finding | numbers | evidence level | source ids |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Video-conferencing search task (static images, 20 observers per experiment). Exp 1 (find highlighted speaker), target-present time: blank 0.61 s, mock scene 0.66 s, identical 0.74 s, varied 0.78 s (varied about +170 ms, +28%); target-absent: blank 0.74 s vs varied 1.15 s (+55%). Exp 2 (find raised-hand symbol): present 0.58 s blank vs 1.01 s varied (+74%); absent 0.81 s vs 1.86 s (+130%). | Feature Congestion clutter: blank 1.92, mock 2.45, varied and identical 3.24 (Exp 1); r between clutter and search time 0.55 to 0.66; error rate up to 0.25 in the worst cell (set size 25, identical background, target absent) | study | G08 |
| Same study: the clutter effect looked weak at set size 4 and strong at larger set sizes; backgrounds sharing the target's colour made targets harder to find. Implication for effects: a pickup or threat sharing hue with surrounding effects loses the search benefit. | weak at set size 4 | study | G08 |
| Human clutter ratings (10-point scale) rose from 3.98 to 7.05 when item count went from low to high; Feature Congestion alone correlates with human ratings at rho 0.60 and is the strongest single predictor (39% of rating variance); four metrics together explain 45%. Spatial disorganisation raised clutter more at high item counts (the fetched summary flagged a means inconsistency in this sub-claim, so treat it as unverified). [V: corrected - the item-count means 3.98 and 7.05 are reported in the paper. 39% is the unique contribution (sr2) of Feature Congestion inside the four-metric model, not its standalone R2; 45% is the four-metric total.] | 3.98 to 7.05; rho 0.60; 39%; 45% | study | G07 |
| Rosenholtz clutter family: Feature Congestion, Subband Entropy, Edge Density computed on any image; they track search performance; colour variability raises clutter and only Feature Congestion captures that. Practical: the agent can score a screenshot with a Feature Congestion style measure (local variance in colour, luminance and orientation) as an automatic clutter proxy. | measure definitions; no cut-off | study (2007; confirmed in use in 2025 and 2026 papers) | G09, G07, G08 |
| Attention capacity: central storage 3 to 5 items (abstract wording; body says chunks) in young adults (Cowan 2010); people can track four or more moving targets (Cavanagh and Alvarez 2005); a 2024 meta-analysis says the target count moderates tracking skill but its abstract gives no value. Candidate rule (inference): about 4 distinct, simultaneously relevant effects per player at a moment (own action, nearest threat, pickup, one ambient); anything beyond must be ambient and low in salience. Caveat: these are capacity limits for tracking or remembering items, not a measured effect-count threshold. [V: confirmed - both numbers and years] [V: corrected - the "about 4 effects" rule is inference only; (d) is OPEN for effect counts because no source measures effects.] | 3 to 5; "four or more" | study (pre-2020 for both numbers) with inference for the rule | G11, G12, G13 |
| Game-specific evidence: a 2026 review proposes enemy density and visible threat count as variables for testing in commercial games and reports no new clutter data. A Europe PMC title search for 2020 to 2026 game plus clutter, effects or distractor plus target detection studies found 15 titles, none testing effect clutter. | Effect screen coverage budget (%) | No studio number. | Render fixed camera shots with N blasts; difference image vs no-effects gives % of pixels changed (coverage) and luminance histogram. Task: find a pickup (and read a threat) while coverage is swept 5, 10, 20, 35, 50%. Knee in time-to-find and error rate = our budget. Keep a check against the 5.6 to 14% above-white highlight share (G17) as a starting guess. |
| Overdraw layers and ms on phones | No Roblox or studio figure; Arm scale is for Mali tools. | Stack k emitters (k = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16) over the same screen area at fixed particle size; read `Stats.RenderGPUFrameTime` on a real low-end Android phone; plot ms vs k and vs covered pixels. Compare to Arm's 2.5x "high" and 10x "too much" anchors. |
| Effect to scene brightness ratio | No game rule found. | Place the same effect on stages of different mean luminance; sweep `Lighting.ExposureCompensation` and particle Brightness/size in 0.5 stop steps; measure effect-focus luminance over local background (relative luminance and the 3:1 W3C floor); find the lowest ratio at which time-to-notice stays flat. Record per-stage value. |
